decks.name: LeetCode #21 - Merge Two Sorted Lists
decks.description: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list

cards.question: Merge Two Sorted Lists: You are given the heads of two sorted linked lists list1 and list2. Merge the two lists into one sorted list. The list should be made by splicing together the nodes of the first two lists. Return the head of the merged linked list.

solutions.name: Iteration
solutions.explanation: Use a dummy node to build the merged list. Maintain a pointer that tracks the current end of the merged list. While both lists have nodes, compare their values and append the smaller one to the merged list, advancing that list's pointer. After one list is exhausted, append the remaining nodes from the other list. This approach uses constant space and is efficient.

solutions.timeDescription: Linear time where n is the length of list1 and m is the length of list2. We visit each node in both lists exactly once.
solutions.spaceDescription: Constant space. Only uses a few pointers to track positions. The merged list reuses existing nodes.
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: For list1=[1,2,4] and list2=[1,3,4]: Create dummy node. Compare 1 and 1, append list1's 1, advance list1 to 2. Compare 2 and 1, append list2's 1, advance list2 to 3. Compare 2 and 3, append list1's 2, advance list1 to 4. Compare 4 and 3, append list2's 3, advance list2 to 4. Compare 4 and 4, append list1's 4, advance list1 to null. Append remaining list2's 4. Result: 1->1->2->3->4->4.

solutions.name: Recursion
solutions.explanation: Recursively merge the lists by choosing the smaller head node and recursively merging the rest. Base cases: if one list is null, return the other list. Recursive case: compare the head values, attach the smaller node to the result of recursively merging its next node with the other list. This elegant solution naturally handles the merging logic but uses call stack space.

solutions.exampleWalkthrough: For list1=[1,2,4] and list2=[1,3,4]: Compare 1<=1, so recurse with [2,4] and [1,3,4]. Compare 2>1, so recurse with [2,4] and [3,4]. Compare 2<=3, so recurse with [4] and [3,4]. Compare 4>3, so recurse with [4] and [4]. Compare 4<=4, so recurse with [] and [4]. Base case: return [4]. Unwind stack building: 4->4, 3->4->4, 2->3->4->4, 1->2->3->4->4, 1->1->2->3->4->4.
